newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends mixed, volume grim.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends mixed, volume grim.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures see-sawed to end mixed on Monday with prices trapped by fund and origin selling at the top and industry price-fixing at the lows.
Benchmark January rebounded from early session lows of $1,370 a tonne to a high of $1,395 before closing at $1,389, still a $5 loss.
It stopped short of challenging the immediate barrier at $1,400 but looked safe above closely-watched $1,360 support.
Front-month November was $20 firmer at $1,514 on a thin volume of 207 lots.
The Nov/Jan spread, a barometer of nearby supply availability, ballooned again to end at $125 from Friday's close of $101 on the strength of November.
Traders said a further 40 lots were tendered against the expiring November contract following Friday's 21 lots.
Overall turnover reached 2,755 lots. Dealings were extremely dull, lacking fresh fundamental inputs.
"It's a kind of non-event," said one.
In the immediate short-term the market is awaiting latest weekly U.S. certified coffee stocks as well as pending gradings figures due to be released after the close of New York trading on Monday.
But traders expect little or no market reaction unless the stocks show a drastic jump.
The certifieds fell 4,036 60-kg bags to just 1,547 bags a week ago, the lowest levels since New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange started tracking inventories in 1980.
No coffee was reported pending grading or recertification as of last week.
Looking ahead, some analysts said the London market could consolidate at current levels.
"We still believe that a bottom seems to be forming in London, even if there is considerable ground for the November premium to narrow," broker GNI said.
Traders said funds could cover shorts if prices attempted upmoves but supply pressures, mainly from Asia and Africa, were likely to cap any substantial rally.
